items.title: 1 dead, 4 critically injured after building collapse in New York City
items.summary_auto: Firefighters dug through the rubble of a three-story building in Brooklyn on Wednesday after it collapsed at the edge of a construction site, killing at least one person and trapping others beneath the wreckage.

items.title: Mississippi's Scott Colom secures Senate seat in another midterm win for Democrats
items.summary_auto: Mississippi Democrat Scott Colom will be the state's first Black senator since the post-Civil War Reconstruction era. Colom's victory also offers Democrats an unexpected boost in their effort to win control of the U.S. Senate.

items.title: Martin Luther King Jr.'s handwritten draft of 'I Have a Dream' speech found in desk drawer
items.summary_auto: The day Martin Luther King Jr. stood on the steps of the Lincoln Memorial and delivered his iconic "I Have A Dream" speech is forever etched in the annals of history. But the night before — when the U.S. civil rights leader stayed up alone in his hotel room scribbling his now-famous words on a yellow notepad — was a moment lost to time. Until now.

items.title: Heritage Minute filmed in Wainwright honours fallen Canadian soldier
items.summary_auto: Capt. Jon Snyder received a Star of Military Valour for his leadership and bravery when his team was attacked in Afghanistan in 2008. The Heritage Minute was filmed at CFB Wainwright and the surrounding area over the summer.

items.title: Canada says Russian hockey players with visas will still be barred from world junior championship
items.summary_auto: The federal government says Russian hockey players will not be permitted to compete at next month's world junior championship in Alberta, even if they already hold valid Canadian visas.

items.title: Jays' Anthony Santander stays quiet after team asks him to publicly address anti-Muslim social media posts
items.summary_auto: The Toronto Blue Jays have asked Anthony Santander to publicly address the controversy sparked by his decision to share anti-Muslim posts on social media. So far, the veteran outfielder has remained quiet and hasn't issued an apology.

items.title: Halifax’s Brian Ahern, who produced albums by Anne Murray and Johnny Cash, dead at 81
items.summary_auto: A Halifax-born music producer who played a big role in helping encourage fellow Bluenoser Anne Murray to pursue a career in music and later produced albums by artists such as Johnny Cash and Emmylou Harris is being remembered for the mark he left on the music industry.

items.title: Various beers under Molson Coors banner recalled Canada-wide
items.summary_auto: Various beers, both alcoholic and non-alcoholic, under the Molson Coors banner have been recalled across Canada due to pieces of metal, according to Health Canada.

items.title: Deadline nears to claim piece of $11-million CIBC mutual funds settlement
items.summary_auto: Investors who held units of a CIBC mutual fund or a Renaissance mutual fund on or before Sept. 5, 2025 might be eligible for compensation. The deadline to apply is Nov. 18.

items.title: Quebec government to table bill restricting access to English-language colleges
items.summary_auto: Next year will mark half a century since the adoption of Quebec's Charter of the French Language, and the Parti Québécois government intends to mark the milestone by reforming the law, says Pascal Bérubé, the minister of the French language.

items.title: Camps destroyed in 2 Israeli military strikes on Gaza City
items.summary_auto: Video shows the moment an Israeli military strike struck near a displacement camp south of Gaza City on Nov. 10. It followed a warning call to a resident of the camp and a smaller drone strike.

items.title: Millions of workers strike across Spain as citizens protest soaring housing costs
items.summary_auto: Millions of Spanish workers shut down businesses and public transportation across the eurozone's fourth largest economy on Wednesday before thousands took to the streets of major cities in a nationwide protest over soaring rents and real estate prices.

items.title: B.C. search-and-rescue mule using his nose to help solve Arizona cold case
items.summary_auto: A British Columbia mule with a nose that knows is helping investigators trying to crack a missing persons cold case in Arizona.

items.title: Father of baby who was rescued after being buried alive is charged with attempted murder
items.summary_auto: A missing 11-month-old infant was rescued Tuesday after being buried alive in a dog crate in South Carolina. His father has been charged with attempted murder.

items.title: TV providers say Rogers' Monday hockey move inflates prices, 'erodes' sports viewing
items.summary_auto: A trio of television providers are accusing Rogers Communications Inc. of violating competition rules and inflating Canadian sports fans' bills by moving Monday night hockey broadcasts exclusively to its Sportsnet Plus streaming service for this NHL season.

items.title: Pilot killed in plane crash during Remembrance Day event in Quebec's Beauce region
items.summary_auto: Wednesday's fatal crash took place in a wooded area close to the local airport in Saint-Georges, Que., about 100 kilometres south of Quebec City.

items.title: 3 arrested after assault near Guelph, Ont., homecoming street party
items.summary_auto: Police in Guelph say three men have been charged with assault after two people were assaulted at a commercial plaza near where an unsanctioned street party was held the weekend of the university's homecoming.

items.title: Canada beats Finland 2-0, stays perfect heading into women's worlds quarterfinals
items.summary_auto: Canada completed the preliminary round at the women's ice hockey world championship with a perfect record after blanking Finland 2-0 on Wednesday.

items.title: Spaniards shut down country over high housing prices
items.summary_auto: People across Spain have shut down businesses, factories and the country’s rail system as part of a general strike. The action comes as many in the country grapple with rising rents and home ownership costs.

items.title: Did Stellantis violate its deals with the feds? Funding contract provided exceptions around Brampton
items.summary_auto: On Tuesday, Prime Minister Mark Carney called Stellantis' now-confirmed plans to sell an automotive assembly plant in Brampton, Ont., "a betrayal" of the global automaker's "obligations to Canada and by extension to all Canadians."

items.title: Jim Jordan, once called a 'legislative terrorist' by a top Republican, will now lead the party in U.S. House
items.summary_auto: The Republicans may have just lost control of the House of Representatives in resounding fashion, but they signalled Tuesday they may not be in a conciliatory mood with Democrats, picking combative Ohio Rep. Jim Jordan as their leader in the chamber.

items.title: Sask. WW II vet says laughter helped him live to 100
items.summary_auto: One of increasingly few surviving Second World War veterans, John Watson still attends all the Remembrance Day ceremonies in Swift Current, Sask. He also recently returned to the Netherlands to mark the anniversary of its liberation.

items.title: Sleeping driver in self-driving vehicle woken up, stopped and charged in Ottawa
items.summary_auto: Provincial police in Ottawa said they stopped and charged a driver who was asleep in her self-driving Tesla during Tuesday rush hour on Highway 417.

items.title: Solemn Remembrance Day ceremonies in Alberta pay tribute to Wainwright's fallen soldiers
Remembrance Day 2026: Canadians remember veterans, fallen soldiers in shadow of Wainwright tragedy
items.summary_auto: As Canadians gather across the country for Remembrance Day ceremonies on Wednesday, Prime Minister Mark Carney said he wants them to know that the act of remembering itself is "an act of vigilance and determination."

items.title: Flooding prompts evacuation order for part of Pemberton as storm batters B.C.
items.summary_auto: The Village of Pemberton issued an evacuation order for a number of properties due to flooding on Wednesday, as heavy rain continued to pound parts of British Columbia.

items.title: The remarkable story behind the secret Canadian guerrilla force you've never heard of
Joining lawsuit, Kennedy family members say Trump's arch would be 'denigration' of JFK, RFK plots at Arlington
items.summary_auto: Nine family members of the Kennedy political dynasty are asking a judge to block U.S. President Donald Trump's plan to build a towering memorial arch, saying the 76-metre structure would cast a shadow over their relatives' gravesites at Arlington National Cemetery.

items.title: Why the first U-boat to surrender in North America landed in this N.S. town
items.summary_auto: Speaking through an interpreter, the U-boat's commander said he would 'very much' like to stay in Canada or the U.S.

items.title: Congo's Ebola outbreak tops 11,000 cases as disease keeps spreading
items.summary_auto: The latest Health Ministry data showed 11,042 people have been infected by the deadly virus that has now killed 5,387, nearly half of those infected, in the country's deadliest outbreak.

items.title: 3 dead, driver arrested after vehicle plows into pedestrians in Los Angeles
items.summary_auto: The 61-year-old driver of a minivan that killed three people when it  crashed outside a Los Angeles metro station during rush hour was arrested on three counts of murder, a police spokesperson said Wednesday.

items.title: Film seeks to highlight work documenting French cave Canadian WW I soldiers called home
items.summary_auto: Last September, men in uniforms dating back to the First World War descended the narrow and slippery steps in the dark to visit Maison Blanche souteraine in northern France. It’s part of a documentary highlighting the work of non-profit Canadigm.

items.title: This veteran thinks his brain cancer is linked to his deployment. He pushed for special benefits — and won
items.summary_auto: It took three attempts for a retired military officer diagnosed with a rare brain cancer to receive special benefits from Veterans Affairs Canada. Bruce Mayo researched and found others with the same diagnosis who also served in Southwest Asia. Mayo wants Canada to change its presumptive injury list, putting it in line with U.S. policy.

items.title: Canadian family finds long-lost WW II baby in England after 80 years
items.summary_auto: Rod Anderson grew up in the United Kingdom always wondering who his father was. At 81 years old, he received a call out of the blue this year that stunned him. It turns out his father was a Canadian soldier stationed in Britain during the Second World War. A family in New Brunswick spent almost 20 years trying to find him.

items.title: Stacy Keach, stage actor and Mike Hammer star, dead at 85
items.summary_auto: Stacy Keach, one of America's finest stage actors who became best known for playing scruffy private eye Mike Hammer on TV and whose career was nearly derailed after he was imprisoned in 1984 for trying to smuggle cocaine into Britain, died Tuesday. He was 85.
